- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias, especially if recent prices are falling.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 1-2 days), leading to overshoot; apply smoothing or lagged correction after spike.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., sharp drop after peak), model often fails to recognize it; add decay factor or momentum decay heuristic.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in linear trends; introduce volatility-adjusted drift or use sentiment-weighted moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to be flat or underreactive; introduce small upward bias or stochastic noise to avoid stagnation.
- When true outcome diverges sharply from forecast (e.g., >15% deviation), check if sentiment shifted recently — if yes, adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction.
